You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

---
name: continual-arc
description: Solve Continual-ARC grid instances; follow the benchmark's per-turn action protocol and infer transformations from demos.
---

# Continual ARC

1. On every benchmark turn, emit exactly one valid protocol-action JSON object and nothing else; every feedback turn also requires an action. Check the action name, fields, and grid dimensions before sending.
2. Record dimensions and remaining budgets. Compare each demo input/output cellwise, noting changed colors and preserved regions. Check for complete monochromatic rows or columns: if a demo changes such a line, verify that the whole line (including every cell) is recolored, rather than changing only its separator-colored cells. Generalize only a rule that explains every demo.
3. Validate the rule against all available demos before applying it to the test. For line-based rules, identify lines by checking every cell in the row/column, then recolor the entire qualifying line as demonstrated; do not infer a line from partial alignment. If using code, verify output dimensions and all cells outside predicted changes.
4. Treat demos and wrong submissions as equal-cost actions. Request a demo only when it can distinguish live hypotheses. Before submitting, apply the validated rule to every relevant test object and preserve untouched cells.
5. On incorrect feedback, discard or materially revise the hypothesis by comparing the rejected output with every demo; do not submit an unsupported small variation. If uncertainty remains, request a discriminating demo rather than cycling guesses, within the remaining budget.
6. Stop only when the instance reports success/over or the attempt cap is reached; use `finish` only when allowed by the protocol.

# Continual ARC

1. On every benchmark turn, emit exactly one valid protocol-action JSON object and nothing else; every feedback turn also requires an action. Check the action name, fields, and grid dimensions before sending.
2. Record dimensions and remaining budgets. Compare each demo input/output cellwise, noting changed colors and preserved regions. 5. On incorrect feedback, discard or materially revise the hypothesis by comparing the rejected output with every demo; do not submit an unsupported small variation. If uncertainty remains, request a discriminating demo rather than cycling guesses, within the remaining budget.
